Mike (app-team): Hey team, embeddings endpoint started failing for one of our batch jobs after a deploy. We get a 400 with "dimension mismatch". Haven't changed model - using our usual text-embedding-3-small. Any ideas?

Alicia (Support): Hi Mike — can you paste the request body and the exact error? Also which client / language?

Mike (app-team): Node axios. Payload looks like: ```json
{
  "inputs": [0.12, -0.03, ... 512 items ...] // single vector
}
```
Error response: ```json
{
  "error": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 512"
}
```

Devon (Support): Hmm — model expecting 1536. Are you sure the model param is still set to text-embedding-3-small in the request? Also your inputs field looks like a flat array, not a list of inputs. For batch we expect [[...], [...]] for multiple items, and ["single string"] for raw text.

Mike (app-team): We're passing raw vectors precomputed client-side from an older encoder. We never changed model name in our config. Request snippet: ```js
axios.post(url + '/embeddings', {
  model: process.env.EMB_MODEL,
  input: vec // vec is a Float32Array converted to array
})
```
Where process.env.EMB_MODEL == "text-embedding-3-small" as before.

Alicia (Support): Two quick checks: 1) Is the client definitely sending a list-of-inputs vs single input? The API will interpret a raw numeric array as a single embedding attempt rather than a batched request, so shape matters. 2) Confirm what encoder produced that 512-d vector — it might be a different model (older local model) and not compatible with the serving model.

ingest-bot: Detected repeated 400s from ip 34.122.x.x to /v1/embeddings (count 14 in 5m) :warning:

Devon (Support): Can you run a quick curl to repro with the same payload? Example: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":[0.1,0.2,...]}'
```
If that returns the same dimension error we can escalate.

Mike (app-team): Ran it, same error. But odd: when I wrap the vector in another array like `input: [[0.1,0.2,...]]` it returns success (embedding id + vectors returned). So behavior changes based on nesting.

Alicia (Support): That matches shape misinterpretation. The API supports two modes: passing text (string) or a list of inputs for batch (each input either string or array of floats). If you pass a plain array of numbers the server treats that as a text tokenization input (bad) OR tries to interpret as a single token sequence causing mismatched dimension expectations. The short fix: always pass a list of inputs for numeric vectors: `input: [[...]]` even for single-item requests.

Jay (Eng): Jumping in — thanks for the clear repro. Two things: 1) The server-side validator expects nested array shape for batched numeric embeddings and will compute model dims based on the requested model. 2) There's an ambiguity we should fix in the client surface: sending a bare numeric array should yield a clearer client-side validation error.

Jay (Eng): Quick debugging notes from logs: request 1792000032 from Mike's IP had payload with "input": [512 numbers]. Router forwarded it and the embeddings service attempted to treat it as text input and ended up with dimension 1536 expectation mismatch. When payload was [[512 numbers]] it mapped to numeric batch path and succeeded.

Devon (Support): Is there any chance model param got overridden to a 1536-d large model on server? Mike said env var was unchanged.

Jay (Eng): Checked rollout flags — no change. The root cause is client shape. Two proposed fixes: (A) short-term: ask Mike to wrap inputs when sending vectors; (B) medium: add a defensive validation on the API gateway that rejects bare numeric arrays with 400 + clear message like "numeric embedding vectors must be sent as a list of vectors: [[...]]"; (C) longer: update SDKs to auto-wrap Float32Array/number[] into [[...]] for single-item numeric inputs.

Alicia (Support): I've communicated (A) to the customer as immediate mitigation. Can we get (B) as a low-risk change? Would cut down on confusing errors.

Jay (Eng): Agreed. I'll open a quick PR to the gateway validator to detect top-level numeric arrays and return helpful error + docs link. Patch ETA ~ end of day. Also will add a note in the API docs about input shapes and examples for both text and numeric vectors.

ingest-bot: Created ticket RED-emb-427 for gateway validation rule (priority: P2).

Mike (app-team): One follow-up — when we send a batch of 32 vectors as `input: [[...],[...],...]` throughput drops ~20% compared to a previous flat-array format we used. Any thoughts?

Devon (Support): We saw similar reports. Can you share your exact payload size and how you're serializing (JSON array of floats vs Base64)?

Mike (app-team): We're using JSON arrays of floats. Each vector ~512 numbers, batch size 32.

Jay (Eng): When batching numeric arrays as nested arrays JSON payloads get large and parsing cost + memory churn can reduce throughput. Two mitigations: 1) prefer binary payloads (we support NDArray protobuf / base64 compact) for large batches, 2) use smaller batch sizes or chunking with concurrent requests. Also ensure you're using HTTP/2 and connection reuse.

Alicia (Support): I added links to docs and a snippet for base64 compressed vectors. Also suggested they try batch size 8/16 to see perf curve.

Mike (app-team): Great, wrapping single vectors fixed the immediate error and switching to batch size 16 + connection reuse regained perf. Thanks.

Jay (Eng): Follow-ups for us: PR for gateway validator, SDK auto-wrap behavior, add a perf doc for numeric batch best practices. I'll add tasks to RED-emb-427.

Devon (Support): Closing loop with customer now — marking thread for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

Alicia (Support): Mike, feel free to reopen if anything else pops up. Glad that was an easy fix. :party_parrot:
